To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transplantation of VEGF and/or IGF-I expressing bone marrow cells (BMC) reduces apoptosis, maximizes survival of transplanted cells, and enhances left ventricular function.

transplantation of bone marrow cell (BM) expressing both vascular endothelial growth (VEGF) and insulin-like growth factor (IGF-I), maximizes transplanted cell retention and reduces cell death in infarcted rat hearts.

transplantation of vascular endothelium growth factor- and insulin-like growth factor I-expressing bone marrow cells reduces cell apoptosis, maximizes cell survival, and improves left ventricular function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the combination of VEGF and insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I), delivered via bone marrow cell transplantation, on the heart.
the development of a novel gene therapy approach for the treatment of heart failure.
the use of stem cells for the repair of damaged or diseased heart muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of multimodal cell-based gene transfer therapy is a promising and potentially effective approach to enhance the benefits of cell therapy in heart failure patients.
the use of multimodal gene therapy, which is the use of two or more genes, is superior to the use of a single gene in the treatment of ischemic cardiomyopathy.
the combination of VEGF and IGFI is the best strategy for cell transplantation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined delivery of VEGF and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) by transplanted bone marrow cells is more efficacious than either alone for the treatment of heart failure.
we have developed a novel approach to cell therapy for heart disease, and this approach may be more effective than other cell therapy approaches.
we have shown that the combination of VEGF and IGFI gene therapy maximizes transplanted cell viability, reduces apoptosis, and enhances LV function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of VEGF and insulin-like growth factor I gene therapy is more efficacious than VEGF or IGF-I alone for improving cardiac function after myocardial infarction.
the combined use of IGF-I and angiogenic growth factors may be a useful approach to maximize the benefits of stem cell transplantation.
the combination of VEGF and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is superior to either one alone for the enhancement of ventricular function after transplantation.
